passages.original: 106 Nam Immensitatem divinitatis Filii Dei ma. nifesta prædicatione, et eloquiorum divinorum attestatione, beatus martyr Cyprianus affirmat in cpislola de Oratione Dominica, dicens : « Denique magisterio suo Dominus secreto nos orare præcepit, in abditis et secretis loci., in cubiculis ipsis, quod magis convenit fidei; ut sciamus Deum ubique esse præsentem, audire omnes et videre, et majestatis, suæ plenitudine in abdita quoque et occulta penetrare, sicut scriptum est: Ego Deus approximans, et non Deus de longinquo. Si absconditus fuerit homo in absconditis, ego crgo non videbo eum?
passages.english: For the blessed martyr Cyprian affirms the immensity of the divinity of the Son of God by clear proclamation and by the testimony of the divine sayings, in [his] letter On the Lord's Prayer, saying: "Finally, by his teaching the Lord commanded us to pray in secret, in hidden and secluded places, in our very bedchambers, which is more fitting to faith; so that we may know that God is present everywhere, hears and sees all, and by the fullness of his majesty penetrates even into hidden and secret places, as it is written: I am a God who draws near, and not a God from afar. If a man has hidden himself in hidden places, shall I then not see him?
passages.notes: Scanning errors corrected: 'ma. nifesta' as manifesta, 'cpislola' as epistola, 'loci.' as locis, 'crgo' as ergo. The quotation is Jeremiah 23:23–24, which continues in the following context.

passages.original: " Simile quiddam beatus Cyprianus etiam ad Tybaritanos scribens de Filii Dei immensitale, testatur his verbis: Solus non est, cui Christus in fuga comes est; solus non est, qui templum Dei servans, ubicunque fuerit, sine Domino non est, et si fugientem in solitudine ac montibus latro oppresserit, fera invaserit, fames aut sitis, aut frigus afflixerit, vel per maria præ. cipiti navigatione properantem, tempestas aut procella submerserit, spectat militem suum Christus ubicunque.
passages.english: The blessed Cyprian, writing also to the Thibaritans, bears witness to something similar concerning the immensity of the Son of God in these words: He is not alone who has Christ as companion in flight; he is not alone who, keeping the temple of God, wherever he may be, is not without the Lord. And if a robber should overpower him as he flees in the wilderness and the mountains, if a wild beast should attack [him], if hunger or thirst or cold should afflict [him], or if a storm or tempest should sink him as he hastens across the seas in headlong voyage, Christ watches over his soldier wherever [he is].
passages.notes: The sentence continues into the following context ('pugnantem', i.e. 'fighting'), so the last clause is completed there: 'watches his soldier fighting wherever [he is]'. 'Tybaritanos' is taken as the people of Thibaris, to whom Cyprian's Letter 58 is addressed. Scanning errors corrected: 'immensitale' as immensitate, 'præ. cipiti' as præcipiti.
